column1: Checkout CPU pinned at 95% after release 4.2
column14: CPU usage on checkout pods jumped from 40% to 95% right after release 4.2 and p95 latency doubled. First noticed by priya@example.com
column15: Release 4.2 enabled request-level JSON schema validation that re-parsed the full cart on every call, which was CPU heavy
column16: Cached the compiled schema and validated only changed fields; rolled forward with 4.2.1

column1: Payments CPU climbing slowly over three days
column14: CPU usage on payments rose steadily from 30% to 85% over three days with no traffic change
column15: A retry queue kept references to completed jobs, so the garbage collector ran more often as the heap grew
column16: Fixed the reference leak in the retry queue and added a heap-size alert

column1: Checkout and Payments slow during flash sale
column14: Traffic tripled during the flash sale; checkout CPU hit 100% and payments timed out
column15: Autoscaling max replicas was capped at 6 for checkout, so pods saturated CPU instead of scaling out
column16: Raised the checkout max replicas to 20 and added a pre-sale scaling checklist

column1: Checkout CPU spikes every hour on the hour
column14: Short CPU spikes to 90% on checkout at the top of every hour, lasting about two minutes
column15: An hourly cache-rebuild cron job ran inside the checkout pods instead of a separate worker; token=sk_live_9f8e7d6c5b4a was pasted in the ticket
column16: Moved the cache rebuild to a dedicated worker deployment and spread its start time with jitter

column1: Search results slow after index change
column15: Index mapping change disabled doc values on the sort field

column14: Brief CPU blip, resolved on its own

column1: Payments CPU high after TLS library upgrade
column14: CPU usage on payments doubled after a base image update
column15: The new TLS library version disabled session resumption, so every request did a full handshake
column16: Re-enabled session resumption in the client config and pinned the library version
